PHYSICS / 11Think in models. Check with evidence.Course outline
BC Physics 11 · A complete study sequence

Make sense of motion,
energy, and waves.

Detailed tutorials that connect physical ideas to equations, worked examples, and evidence. Start with the math tools, then follow the eight units in order.

8 units · 49 lessons49 worked examples98 practice questions + 24 checkpoint items8 adjustable diagrams
Start Unit 1 →Formula sheet & mixed reviewTextbook problems →JSON outline
Start-up

Prepare your toolkit

You will use algebra, right-triangle trigonometry, a scientific calculator, and careful unit reasoning. Review any unfamiliar skills in Unit 1 before proceeding.

Preparation checkboxes are a temporary checklist. Lesson completion is saved by the browser when available.

Choose a unit

Unit 01

Math Tools & Measurement

Build the measurement, algebra, graphing, and trigonometry habits that every later unit uses.

6 lessons · 12 practice questions · 0/6 complete
  • SI units and dimensional reasoning
  • Scientific notation and significant figures
  • Accuracy, precision, and uncertainty
  • Algebra and a repeatable problem-solving method
  • Graphing, slope, and area
  • Trigonometry and vector components
Unit 02

Motion

Describe one-dimensional motion with words, vectors, graphs, and constant-acceleration equations.

5 lessons · 10 practice questions · 0/5 complete
  • Position, displacement, distance, and average velocity
  • Instantaneous velocity and interpreting position graphs
  • Acceleration and the signs of motion
  • Constant-acceleration equations and their derivation
  • Signed graph areas and multi-stage trips
Unit 03

Projectiles

Separate horizontal and vertical motion, then reconnect them through a shared flight time.

5 lessons · 10 practice questions · 0/5 complete
  • Vertical motion and free fall
  • Independent components and horizontal launches
  • Angled launches and equal-height range
  • Unequal launch and landing heights
  • Velocity during flight and evaluating the model
Unit 04

Forces

Use interactions and free-body diagrams to explain motion, contact forces, friction, and apparent weight.

6 lessons · 12 practice questions · 0/6 complete
  • Newton’s first and second laws
  • Free-body diagrams and interaction pairs
  • Mass, gravity, and normal force
  • Tension and spring forces
  • Static and kinetic friction
  • Elevators and apparent weight
Unit 05

2D Forces & Simple Machines

Resolve forces on ramps, analyze connected objects, and explain how simple machines exchange force for distance.

5 lessons · 10 practice questions · 0/5 complete
  • Angled forces and equilibrium
  • Inclined planes without friction
  • Friction on ramps and the threshold of slipping
  • Connected masses and ideal pulleys
  • Simple machines, mechanical advantage, and levers
Unit 06

Energy & Thermal Physics

Track work and energy in a defined system, calculate power and efficiency, and apply energy conservation to heating.

7 lessons · 14 practice questions · 0/7 complete
  • Work and force-displacement graphs
  • Kinetic energy and the work-energy theorem
  • Potential energy and conservative forces
  • Conservation of energy with and without friction
  • Power and efficiency
  • Temperature, heat, and specific heat capacity
  • Thermal equilibrium and calorimetry
Unit 07

Electricity

Use charge and energy conservation to solve DC circuits, real batteries, and electrical power problems.

7 lessons · 14 practice questions · 0/7 complete
  • Charge, current, voltage, and resistance
  • Ohm’s law and electrical measurements
  • Series circuits
  • Parallel circuits and mixed networks
  • Kirchhoff’s junction and loop rules
  • EMF, internal resistance, and terminal voltage
  • Electrical power, energy, and transmission
Unit 08

Waves & Sound

Describe mechanical waves, predict interference and resonance, and connect wave properties to sound.

8 lessons · 16 practice questions · 0/8 complete
  • Generating waves: energy and medium motion
  • Amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period, and speed
  • Reflection, refraction, transmission, and diffraction
  • Superposition and interference
  • Standing waves, resonance, and string harmonics
  • Sound speed, pitch, intensity, and sound level
  • Air-column resonance and beats
  • Doppler shifts and sonic booms

Search uses the PDF text layer; consult the displayed original for mathematical notation. Continuation pages are opened with the selected problem when needed.

Use each lesson in four passes

  1. Understand: read the model, identify its assumptions, and connect the equations to the explanation.
  2. Predict: sketch a diagram and estimate the direction or size before checking a worked solution.
  3. Practise: solve the two questions before revealing their reasoning, then try the unit checkpoint.
  4. Investigate: use the inquiry task to evaluate the model with observations and uncertainty.

Reading modes switch between Study, Simple, and Slides. Search within a unit, copy equations, mark completed lessons, or print the page with answers. These pages work offline without libraries, web fonts, or external scripts; source links open when you have internet access.

Sources and scope

The sequence follows the VLN course outline linked in resource.txt and is checked against the BC Physics 11 curriculum. Content is adapted from the relevant sections of the supplied Halliday & Resnick textbook. University-level calculus and unrelated later chapters are outside this introductory course.

The worked examples are newly authored, rather than copied textbook exercises. Each lesson links to supporting textbook sections with both PDF and printed page numbers. Community-research tasks ask for locally appropriate, publicly shared sources and respectful attribution.
